findings.summary: __getstate__ now returns a dict and __setstate__ assumes a dict, so unpickling old tuple-state slotted instances raises TypeError or silently yields an empty object; __setstate__ should handle tuple state with the old zip logic.
No test loads a tuple-format (old) pickle, so the backward-compatibility regression would not be caught.
New module-level class A with parametrize('cls', [A]) is redundant and its generic global name could collide with other classes in the file.
